title: Postal Service Clerks
description: Perform any combination of tasks in a United States Postal Service (USPS) post office, such as receive letters and parcels; sell postage and revenue stamps, postal cards, and stamped envelopes; fill out and sell money orders; place mail in pigeon holes of mail rack or in bags; and examine mail for correct postage. Includes postal service clerks employed by USPS contractors.

tasks.text: Weigh letters and parcels, compute mailing costs based on type, weight, and destination, and affix correct postage.
Obtain signatures from recipients of registered or special delivery mail.
Check mail to ensure correct postage and that packages and letters are in proper condition for mailing.
Sort incoming and outgoing mail, according to type and destination, by hand or by operating electronic mail-sorting and scanning devices.
Keep money drawers in order, and record and balance daily transactions.
Complete forms regarding changes of address, or theft or loss of mail, or for special services such as registered or priority mail.
Put undelivered parcels away, retrieve them when customers come to claim them, and complete any related documentation.
Transport mail from one work station to another.
Feed mail into postage canceling devices or hand stamp mail to cancel postage.
Sell and collect payment for products such as stamps, prepaid mail envelopes, and money orders.
Register, certify, and insure letters and parcels.
Receive letters and parcels, and place mail into bags.
Respond to complaints regarding mail theft, delivery problems, and lost or damaged mail, filling out forms and making appropriate referrals for investigation.
Answer questions regarding mail regulations and procedures, postage rates, and post office boxes.
Provide assistance to the public in complying with federal regulations of Postal Service and other federal agencies.
Rent post office boxes to customers.
Provide customers with assistance in filing claims for mail theft, or lost or damaged mail.
Order retail items and other supplies for office use.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: Budgeting software.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Delivery operations information system DOIS.

skills.name: Time accounting software
skills.def: Software to submit or manage time accounting for human resources. Examples: Electronic Time Clock ETC.

skills.name: Inventory management software
skills.def: Software to maintain the inventory of businesses including restaurants or retail shops. Examples: Inventory tracking software.

skills.name: Point of sale POS software
